_meta.contract: every consumer replays these against its own evaluator: for each vector, bind the leaf of `dimension` under `family` (null: the leaf is unknown), take verb, identity, group, seats and act from `ctx` (an absent key is unknown), and read the `cell`. `expect` is the answer: a count's doors, authored or counted, the second signers as [{role, member}], `unknown`, `gap`, or null where every arm reads false; `decided_by` is the deciding arm's index. An arm is false if any test is false, else unknown if any test is unknown; an unknown arm before the decider makes the answer unknown. Where the answer is `subject`, `admits` says whether the statement is admitted: true when ctx `iss` equals ctx `sub`, false when it differs, `unknown` when either is absent. A vector with `voice` offers a statement in that role over the row: `admits` is true only when the second_signers answer names the role

keys.leaf: bound from the dimension: the family's non-literal segment values joined by ':', version tail stripped; `{name}` in a value matches one segment
keys.verb: caller-supplied: one of attest, authorize, replace, withdraw, recant
keys.identity: caller-supplied: the identity_type set of the identity the row concerns; holds when it contains a value
keys.group: caller-supplied: the cohort_scope of the group the row is about (family, community, affiliations)
keys.seats: caller-supplied: the group's deciding-seat count at the head the row names; `one` is 1
keys.act: caller-supplied, never a payload member: derived from the statements the row carries; group when the row is the act of a roster under its consensus_protocol, several statements over one payload (CC 2.6.1.9); own when it is one statement by the author
keys.iss: read from the statement: its CWT iss; compared with sub by the authorship value subject
keys.sub: read from the statement: its CWT sub, the attested key
